B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Morningstar describes data pricing as depending on the data package, distribution level, and use case. No per-call MCP charge or MCP-specific quota was found.

Claude for Enterprise connector setup is performed by an administrator. No hosted endpoint rate limits or role-level MCP settings were found.

C_capabilities.depends_on_mcp_version: OAuth protected-resource metadata advertises MCP protocol version 2025-06-18.
C_capabilities.description_what_how: The supplied endpoint POST returned HTTP 401 with “missing authorization — no claims in any metadata path.” Both protected-resource documents identify https://mcp.morningstar.com/mcp as the resource and https://mcp.morningstar.com/mcp as the authorization server; both advertise bearer tokens in the header and scopes_supported ["offline_access", "openid", "email", "profile"]. The authorization-server metadata at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/mcp advertises registration_endpoint https://mcp.morningstar.com/oauth-issuer/register (dynamic client registration), PKCE S256, authorization_code and refresh_token grants, response type code, token endpoint authentication methods client_secret_basic, client_secret_post, and none, and require_pushed_authorization_requests=false. client_id_metadata_document_supported=false; resource_indicators_supported=false. Token lifetime and revocation details were not found.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: OAuth bearer token is sent in the Authorization header; token response structure and lifetime are not in the supplied metadata.
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: Metadata Doc; Dynamic Client Registration. Raw metadata values: bearer_methods_supported=["header"]; scopes_supported=["offline_access","openid","email","profile"]; registration_endpoint="https://mcp.morningstar.com/oauth-issuer/register"; grant_types_supported=["authorization_code","refresh_token"]; code_challenge_methods_supported=["S256"]; token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported=["client_secret_basic","client_secret_post","none"]; require_pushed_authorization_requests=false; client_id_metadata_document_supported=false. Token lifetime/revocation: NOT FOUND.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The seven hosted tools retrieve information according to their official descriptions; official tool annotations such as readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, and openWorldHint were not published. 2. No write or destructive tool or server-enforced confirmation flow is documented; client approval guidance is advice only. 3. OAuth bearer auth uses the identity scopes offline_access, openid, email, and profile; a licensed account is required. Product-role inheritance, org switches, token lifetime/revocation, and client allowlists were not found. 4. No hosted read-only mode, toolset filter, query-free mode, sandbox, or region-specific MCP endpoint was found. 5. No hosted PII masking, secrets treatment, or scope boundaries were documented. 6. No MCP-specific rate limits, quotas, bulk caps, time-range caps, per-call costs, or truncation were found; a Microsoft Power Automate connector page lists 100 calls per connection per 60 seconds for that integration surface. 7. Hosted validation, correction, and unknown-argument behavior are unknown. 8. Hosted audit logs and telemetry are undocumented. 9. The official seven-tool list contains no feedback, rating, reporting, or survey tool; no upsell result behavior was found. 10. Hosted initialize instructions and skills are unavailable. Tool descriptions give functional guidance; for example, the articles tool is not intended for factual security ratings, prices, fair value, or performance. 11. Persistence of agent history or server-side state is undocumented. 12. The hosted tool surface is documented as one flat list; no sub-server or proxy structure was found. Historical local code calls downstream datapoint and retrieval services, but is not established as the hosted implementation. 13. No raw API, arbitrary query, SQL, or script-execution tool appears in the official list.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: An official tool list exists at https://developer.morningstar.com/direct-web-services/documentation/mcp-server/morningstar-mcp-server and names seven tools; the official page gives no separate numeric total. All seven official names are included. No catalogue-only tools were added. Anthropic's Claude connector directory lists six (omitting morningstar-portfolio-analysis-tool); Labsco lists seven; mcp.tc says Morningstar does not show its tools before sign-in; mcp.so has no list to display. The official list takes precedence over the Claude directory's incomplete list.

Returns relevant portions of articles, news, and commentary published on Morningstar.com and other Morningstar products.
Retrieves Morningstar’s AI-ready data for global mutual funds, ETFs, and stocks.
Retrieves the top holdings for a list of mutual funds or ETFs.
Identifies relevant investments and data points to hand off to other tools.

E_aggregated.token_method: The hosted server's tool schemas and initialize instructions are not available without authorization. The archived code is a different implementation and was not used to estimate hosted context.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: Morningstar says its platform provides targeted workflows and certain proprietary IP not available through connectors. The MCP tool list contains research, data retrieval, screening, holdings, and X-Ray analysis tools, but no tools for editing universes or custom data or administering users. Morningstar's Direct Web Services Admin Tool documentation describes interface capabilities to add/remove universe securities, edit/import/export custom data points, and manage user details; these are not documented as MCP actions.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Official documentation directs users to connect through standard MCP clients and authenticate with Morningstar credentials; it does not publish behavioral workflow rules for the hosted tools. A third-party directory recommends client-side approval prompts for any tool that can write, trade, or send, but the official tool list describes read-oriented operations and this recommendation is not a server control.
F_documentation.governance_promises: The product page describes access to “governed, AI-ready data and analytics.” No reviewed Morningstar privacy page or MCP-specific terms could be accessed that explain MCP data retention, processing, deletion, AI training, or audit logging.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The official developer page says the server provides access to Morningstar content and requires a licensed account. The product page describes its data and research as trusted and independent. These are product claims, not measured guarantees about an individual response.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: The access requirement is reflected in the OAuth-protected endpoint and licensed-account documentation. No other reviewed governance promise could be compared against hosted implementation because the endpoint requires authorization and server-side governance details are not published in the accessible materials.

contradictions: The official developer page lists seven tools, including morningstar-portfolio-analysis-tool; Anthropic's Claude connector listing names six and omits that tool. No other name difference was identified.

The archived official repository documents two historical local tools, while current hosted Morningstar documentation lists seven differently named tools. The repository README states it is archived and development takes place outside it; it is not evidence of the deployed endpoint's current tools.
observations_for_research: The protected-resource metadata exposes identity scopes (offline_access, openid, email, profile) rather than tool-specific data scopes; licensing is separately required.

An official archived implementation has operator-fixed US domicile and exchange filters, disables its screener flag, and passes an authorization token as a tool argument. These are properties of that historical local variant, not established hosted-server behavior.

The official hosted documentation is JavaScript-rendered and the prepared local page copy contains only the shell; the indexed official page content was accessible through web search and supplied the full seven-tool list.
notes: Checked links.json, links_check.txt, pages/INDEX.txt, official page copies and their HTML, available script extracts, the official repository copy, and supplied OAuth metadata. The official developer page's local HTML is a JavaScript shell, but its indexed official content provided the complete tool names and descriptions. Hosted endpoint and /install returned 401 without authorization; no login was attempted. The official privacy policy URL returned 403 in the prepared evidence. No public hosted schemas, parameter lists, annotations, initialize instructions, or exact MCP price were found. Unofficial and third-party directories were used only for list cross-checks and clearly labeled contextual evidence.
